subject.title: fix: QueuedFileWriter silently swallows all write errors

question: Should optional QueuedFileWriter diagnostic sinks warn when mkdir or append fails, and what bounded/redacted policy should be accepted?
rationale: The source path is clear, but the reporter narrowed the impact to optional diagnostics and a raw console warning could create noise or leak local diagnostic details.

options.title: Add bounded diagnostic warning
options.body: Approve a deduped warning or debug signal for consecutive write failures that keeps writes non-fatal and avoids sensitive path or payload leakage.

options.title: Keep silent best-effort writes
options.body: Treat diagnostic JSONL persistence as intentionally best-effort and close the issue without adding operator-facing noise.

options.title: Refresh the linked PR first
options.body: Ask a maintainer to decide whether the open conflicting PR should be refreshed, replaced, or closed before any new implementation is queued.

recommendation.title: Add bounded diagnostic warning
recommendation.body: Approve a deduped warning or debug signal for consecutive write failures that keeps writes non-fatal and avoids sensitive path or payload leakage.

likelyOwner.reason: The shared queued writer introduction and repeated adjacent agent-runtime maintenance make this the strongest available routing signal.
